paper.title: Fairness of Exposure in Stochastic Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: FairX setting for stochastic MAB (frequentist, FairX-UCB)
unmapped: learner knows the merit function f mapping mean rewards to positive merit
learner selects a randomized policy each round; regret is measured against the optimal fair policy pi*(a) = f(mu_a)/sum f(mu_a')
fairness regret = cumulative l1 distance between deployed policy and optimal fair policy
settings.definition_quote: we aim to learn a policy $\pi^\star$ which ensures that each arm receives an amount of exposure proportional to its merit ... We thus define the {\em reward regret} ... We thus define the following {\em fairness regret} ... which measures the cumulative $\ell^1$ distance between the deployed policy and the optimal fair policy

settings.name_in_paper: FairX setting for stochastic MAB (Bayesian, FairX-TS)
unmapped: learner knows the merit function f
regret measured against the optimal fair policy; fairness regret = cumulative l1 distance
settings.definition_quote: suppose the mean reward $\Params^\star_a$ of each arm $a$ is independently sampled from standard normal distribution $\Normal(0,1)$, and $\forall t,\Action$  $\Reward_{t,\Action}\sim\Normal(\Params^\star_\Action,1)$

settings.name_in_paper: FairX setting for stochastic MAB (lower bound)
unmapped: learner knows the merit function f
fairness regret = cumulative l1 distance to the optimal fair policy
settings.definition_quote: Let us consider two MAB instances ... where each instance has two arms, and each arm has reward distributions being Gaussian distributions with variance fixed to be $1/2$.

settings.name_in_paper: FairX setting for stochastic linear bandits (FairX-LinUCB)
unmapped: learner knows the merit function f
per-round optimal fair policy pi*_t(a) proportional to f(theta*.x_{t,a}); fairness regret = cumulative l1 distance
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t$, the learner is given a set of context vectors $\Actions_t\subset\mathbb{R}^\Dimension$ representing the arms ... We focus on problems where the number of available arms is finite $\forall t: \lvert\Actions_t\rvert=\NumActions$

settings.name_in_paper: FairX setting for stochastic linear bandits (Bayesian, FairX-LinTS)
unmapped: learner knows the merit function f
per-round optimal fair policy; fairness regret = cumulative l1 distance
settings.definition_quote: suppose each dimension of the true parameter $\Params^\star$ is independently sampled from standard normal distribution $\Normal(0,1)$, $\forall t,a$ $\|\Context_{t,\Action}\|_2\leq 1$, $\eta_t$ is sampled from standard normal distribution $\Normal(0,1)$

conditions: merit function f has minimum merit f_min > 0 (Condition 2)

source.label: theo:fair_UCB_FR
source.quote: Under Condition ~\ref{condi:min_merit} and ~\ref{condi:lip_cont}, suppose $\forall t,\Action: \Reward_{t,\Action}\in[-1,1]$, when $\TimeSteps>\NumActions$, for any $\delta\in(0,1)$, set $\ConfiWidth = \sqrt{2\ln\left(4\TimeSteps\NumActions/\delta\right)}$,  the fairness regret of the \FairXUCB\ algorithm is $\FairnessRegret_\TimeSteps =\widetilde{O}\left( \LipConst\sqrt{\NumActions\TimeSteps}/\MeritMin\right)$ with probability at least $1-\delta$.

results.notes: Fairness regret (l1 distance to optimal fair policy), recorded as quantity other. Step 7 is a non-convex optimisation, so compute not stated as polynomial.

source.label: theo:fair_UCB_RR
source.quote: Suppose $\forall t,\Action: \Reward_{t,\Action}\in[-1,1]$, when $\TimeSteps>\NumActions$, for any $\delta\in(0,1)$, set $\ConfiWidth = \sqrt{2\ln\left(4\TimeSteps\NumActions/\delta\right)}$, the reward regret of the \FairXUCB\ algorithm is $\RewardRegret_\TimeSteps =\widetilde{O}\left( \sqrt{\NumActions\TimeSteps}\right)$ with probability at least $1-\delta$.

results.notes: Reward regret against the optimal fair policy, defined through means; holds with probability 1-delta.

conditions: a 1-Lipschitz merit function with minimum merit 1/sqrt(T) (minimum-merit condition violated)

source.label: theo:lower_bound_min_merit
source.quote: For time horizon $\TimeSteps>0$, there exists a $1$-Lipschitz continuous merit function $f$ where $\min_{\Params} \Merit(\Params) = 1/\sqrt{\TimeSteps}$, such that for any bandit algorithm, there must exist a MAB instance such that the expected fairness regret is at least $\mE\left[\FairnessRegret_\TimeSteps\right] \geq 0.015 \TimeSteps$.

results.notes: Expected fairness regret lower bound; the paper says it also applies to linear bandits via basis-vector embedding.

conditions: a sqrt(T)-Lipschitz merit function with minimum merit 1 (bounded Lipschitz condition violated)

source.label: theo:lower_bound_lip_cont
source.quote: For time horizon $\TimeSteps>0$, there exists a $\sqrt{\TimeSteps}$-Lipschitz continuous merit function $f$ with minimum merit $1$, such that for any bandit algorithm, there must exist a MAB instance such that the expected fairness regret is at least $\mE[\FairnessRegret_\TimeSteps] \geq 0.015 \TimeSteps$.

conditions: merit function has minimum merit f_min > 0 (Condition 2)
mean rewards drawn i.i.d. from N(0,1) prior

source.label: theo:fair_TS_FR
source.quote: Under Condition~\ref{condi:min_merit} and ~\ref{condi:lip_cont}, suppose the mean reward $\Params^\star_a$ of each arm $a$ is independently sampled from standard normal distribution $\Normal(0,1)$, and $\forall t,\Action$  $\Reward_{t,\Action}\sim\Normal(\Params^\star_\Action,1)$, the Bayesian fairness regret of the \FairXTS\ algorithm at any round $\TimeSteps$ is $\text{Bayes}\FairnessRegret_\TimeSteps=\widetilde{O}\left( \LipConst\sqrt{\NumActions\TimeSteps}/\MeritMin \right)$.

results.notes: Bayesian fairness regret (expectation over prior), recorded as quantity other.

conditions: mean rewards drawn i.i.d. from N(0,1) prior

source.label: theo:fair_TS_RR
source.quote: Suppose the mean reward $\Params^\star_a$ of each arm $a$ is independently sampled from standard normal distribution $\Normal(0,1)$, and $\forall t,\Action$  $\Reward_{t,\Action}\sim\Normal(\Params^\star_\Action,1)$, the Bayesian fairness regret of the \FairXTS\ algorithm at any round $\TimeSteps$ is $\text{Bayes}\RewardRegret_\TimeSteps=\widetilde{O}\left( \sqrt{\NumActions\TimeSteps} \right)$.

results.notes: Statement text says 'fairness regret' but the formula and title are Bayesian reward regret.

conditions: merit function has minimum merit f_min > 0 (Condition 2)
tuning: beta_t = (W + sqrt(d ln(1+t/d) + 2 ln(pi^2 t^2/(3 delta))))^2

source.label: theo:fair_LinUCB_FR
source.quote: Under Condition~\ref{condi:min_merit} and~\ref{condi:lip_cont}, suppose $\forall t,a$ $\|\Context_{t,\Action}\|_2\leq 1$, $\eta_t$ is $1$ sub-Gaussian, $\|\Params^{\star}\|_2\leq 1$, set $\lambda=1$, with proper choice of $\beta_t$, the fairness regret at any round $\TimeSteps>0$ is $\FairnessRegret_\TimeSteps=\widetilde{O}\left(\LipConst\Dimension\sqrt{\TimeSteps}/{\MeritMin}\right)$ with high probability.

results.notes: Fairness regret, quantity other. Optimistic step is non-convex.

tuning: beta_t = (W + sqrt(d ln(1+t/d) + 2 ln(pi^2 t^2/(3 delta))))^2

source.label: theo:fair_LinUCB_RR
source.quote: Suppose $\forall t,a$ $\|\Context_{t,\Action}\|_2\leq 1$, $\eta_t$ is $1$ sub-Gaussian, $\|\Params^{\star}\|_2\leq 1$, set $\lambda=1$, with proper choice of $\beta_t$, the reward regret at any round $\TimeSteps>0$ is $\RewardRegret_\TimeSteps=\widetilde{O}\left(\Dimension\sqrt{\TimeSteps}\right)$ with high probability.

results.notes: Reward regret vs per-round optimal fair policy.

conditions: merit function has minimum merit f_min > 0 (Condition 2)

source.label: theo:fair_LinTS_FR
source.quote: Under Condition~\ref{condi:min_merit} and~\ref{condi:lip_cont}, suppose each dimension of the true parameter $\Params^\star$ is independently sampled from standard normal distribution $\Normal(0,1)$, $\forall t,a$ $\|\Context_{t,\Action}\|_2\leq 1$, $\eta_t$ is sampled from standard normal distribution $\Normal(0,1)$, the Bayesian fairness regret of the \FairXLinTS\ algorithm is $\text{Bayes}\FairnessRegret=\widetilde{O}\left(\LipConst\sqrt{\Dimension\TimeSteps}/\MeritMin\right)$.

results.notes: Bayesian fairness regret, quantity other. Proof's lower-order terms include sqrt(K) factors hidden in O_tilde.

source.label: theo:fair_LinTS_RR
source.quote: Suppose each dimension of the true parameter $\Params^\star$ is independently sampled from standard normal distribution $\Normal(0,1)$, $\forall t,a$ $\|\Context_{t,\Action}\|_2\leq 1$, $\eta_t$ is sampled from standard normal distribution $\Normal(0,1)$, the Bayesian reward regret of the \FairXLinTS\ algorithm is $\text{Bayes}\RewardRegret=\widetilde{O}\left( \Dimension\sqrt{\TimeSteps} \right)$.

results.notes: Bayesian reward regret against per-round optimal fair policy.
